[2057](https://docs.rs#2057)    /// Transform the array into `shape`; any shape with the same number of
[2058](https://docs.rs#2058)    /// elements is accepted, but the source array or view must be in standard
[2059](https://docs.rs#2059)    /// or column-major (Fortran) layout.
[2060](https://docs.rs#2060)    ///
[2061](https://docs.rs#2061)    /// **Note** that `.into_shape()` "moves" elements differently depending on if the input array
[2062](https://docs.rs#2062)    /// is C-contig or F-contig, it follows the index order that corresponds to the memory order.
[2063](https://docs.rs#2063)    /// Prefer to use `.to_shape()` or `.into_shape_with_order()`.
[2064](https://docs.rs#2064)    ///
[2065](https://docs.rs#2065)    /// Because of this, the method **is deprecated**. That reshapes depend on memory order is not
[2066](https://docs.rs#2066)    /// intuitive.
[2067](https://docs.rs#2067)    ///
[2068](https://docs.rs#2068)    /// **Errors** if the shapes don't have the same number of elements.<br>
[2069](https://docs.rs#2069)    /// **Errors** if the input array is not c- or f-contiguous.
[2070](https://docs.rs#2070)    ///
[2071](https://docs.rs#2071)    /// ```
[2072](https://docs.rs#2072)    /// use ndarray::{aview1, aview2};
[2073](https://docs.rs#2073)    ///
[2074](https://docs.rs#2074)    /// assert!(
[2075](https://docs.rs#2075)    ///     aview1(&[1., 2., 3., 4.]).into_shape((2, 2)).unwrap()
[2076](https://docs.rs#2076)    ///     == aview2(&[[1., 2.],
[2077](https://docs.rs#2077)    ///                 [3., 4.]])
[2078](https://docs.rs#2078)    /// );
[2079](https://docs.rs#2079)    /// ```
[2080](https://docs.rs#2080)    #[deprecated(note = "Use `.into_shape_with_order()` or `.to_shape()`", since = "0.16.0")]
[2081](https://docs.rs#2081)    pub fn into_shape<E>(self, shape: E) -> Result<ArrayBase<S, E::Dim>, ShapeError>
[2082](https://docs.rs#2082)    where E: IntoDimension
[2083](https://docs.rs#2083)    {
[2084](https://docs.rs#2084)        let shape = shape.into_dimension();
[2085](https://docs.rs#2085)        if size_of_shape_checked(&shape) != Ok(self.parts.dim.size()) {
[2086](https://docs.rs#2086)            return Err(error::incompatible_shapes(&self.parts.dim, &shape));
[2087](https://docs.rs#2087)        }
[2088](https://docs.rs#2088)        // Check if contiguous, if not => copy all, else just adapt strides
[2089](https://docs.rs#2089)        unsafe {
[2090](https://docs.rs#2090)            // safe because arrays are contiguous and len is unchanged
[2091](https://docs.rs#2091)            if self.is_standard_layout() {
[2092](https://docs.rs#2092)                Ok(self.with_strides_dim(shape.default_strides(), shape))
[2093](https://docs.rs#2093)            } else if self.ndim() > 1 && self.raw_view().reversed_axes().is_standard_layout() {
[2094](https://docs.rs#2094)                Ok(self.with_strides_dim(shape.fortran_strides(), shape))
[2095](https://docs.rs#2095)            } else {
[2096](https://docs.rs#2096)                Err(error::from_kind(error::ErrorKind::IncompatibleLayout))
[2097](https://docs.rs#2097)            }
[2098](https://docs.rs#2098)        }
[2099](https://docs.rs#2099)    }
[2100](https://docs.rs#2100)
[2101](https://docs.rs#2101)    /// Transform the array into `shape`; any shape with the same number of
[2102](https://docs.rs#2102)    /// elements is accepted. Array elements are reordered in place if
[2103](https://docs.rs#2103)    /// possible, otherwise they are copied to create a new array.
[2104](https://docs.rs#2104)    ///
[2105](https://docs.rs#2105)    /// If an index ordering is not specified, the default is `RowMajor`.
[2106](https://docs.rs#2106)    ///
[2107](https://docs.rs#2107)    /// # `.to_shape` vs `.into_shape_clone`
[2108](https://docs.rs#2108)    ///
[2109](https://docs.rs#2109)    /// - `to_shape` supports views and outputting views
[2110](https://docs.rs#2110)    /// - `to_shape` borrows the original array, `into_shape_clone` consumes the original
[2111](https://docs.rs#2111)    /// - `into_shape_clone` preserves array type (Array vs ArcArray), but does not support views.
[2112](https://docs.rs#2112)    ///
[2113](https://docs.rs#2113)    /// **Errors** if the shapes don't have the same number of elements.<br>
[2114](https://docs.rs#2114)    pub fn into_shape_clone<E>(self, shape: E) -> Result<ArrayBase<S, E::Dim>, ShapeError>
[2115](https://docs.rs#2115)    where
[2116](https://docs.rs#2116)        S: DataOwned,
[2117](https://docs.rs#2117)        A: Clone,
[2118](https://docs.rs#2118)        E: ShapeArg,
[2119](https://docs.rs#2119)    {
[2120](https://docs.rs#2120)        let (shape, order) = shape.into_shape_and_order();
[2121](https://docs.rs#2121)        let order = order.unwrap_or(Order::RowMajor);
[2122](https://docs.rs#2122)        self.into_shape_clone_order(shape, order)
[2123](https://docs.rs#2123)    }
[2124](https://docs.rs#2124)
[2125](https://docs.rs#2125)    fn into_shape_clone_order<E>(self, shape: E, order: Order) -> Result<ArrayBase<S, E>, ShapeError>
[2126](https://docs.rs#2126)    where
[2127](https://docs.rs#2127)        S: DataOwned,
[2128](https://docs.rs#2128)        A: Clone,
[2129](https://docs.rs#2129)        E: Dimension,
[2130](https://docs.rs#2130)    {
[2131](https://docs.rs#2131)        let len = self._dim().size();
[2132](https://docs.rs#2132)        if size_of_shape_checked(&shape) != Ok(len) {
[2133](https://docs.rs#2133)            return Err(error::incompatible_shapes(self._dim(), &shape));
[2134](https://docs.rs#2134)        }
[2135](https://docs.rs#2135)
[2136](https://docs.rs#2136)        // Safe because the array and new shape is empty.
[2137](https://docs.rs#2137)        if len == 0 {
[2138](https://docs.rs#2138)            unsafe {
[2139](https://docs.rs#2139)                return Ok(self.with_strides_dim(shape.default_strides(), shape));
[2140](https://docs.rs#2140)            }
[2141](https://docs.rs#2141)        }
[2142](https://docs.rs#2142)
[2143](https://docs.rs#2143)        // Try to reshape the array's current data
[2144](https://docs.rs#2144)        match reshape_dim(self._dim(), self._strides(), &shape, order) {
[2145](https://docs.rs#2145)            Ok(to_strides) => unsafe {
[2146](https://docs.rs#2146)                return Ok(self.with_strides_dim(to_strides, shape));
[2147](https://docs.rs#2147)            },
[2148](https://docs.rs#2148)            Err(err) if err.kind() == ErrorKind::IncompatibleShape => {
[2149](https://docs.rs#2149)                return Err(error::incompatible_shapes(self._dim(), &shape));
[2150](https://docs.rs#2150)            }
[2151](https://docs.rs#2151)            _otherwise => {}
[2152](https://docs.rs#2152)        }
[2153](https://docs.rs#2153)
[2154](https://docs.rs#2154)        // otherwise, clone and allocate a new array
[2155](https://docs.rs#2155)        unsafe {
[2156](https://docs.rs#2156)            let (shape, view) = match order {
[2157](https://docs.rs#2157)                Order::RowMajor => (shape.set_f(false), self.view()),
[2158](https://docs.rs#2158)                Order::ColumnMajor => (shape.set_f(true), self.t()),
[2159](https://docs.rs#2159)            };
[2160](https://docs.rs#2160)
[2161](https://docs.rs#2161)            Ok(ArrayBase::from_shape_trusted_iter_unchecked(shape, view.into_iter(), A::clone))
[2162](https://docs.rs#2162)        }
[2163](https://docs.rs#2163)    }
[2164](https://docs.rs#2164)
[2165](https://docs.rs#2165)    /// *Note: Reshape is for `ArcArray` only. Use `.into_shape_with_order()` for
[2166](https://docs.rs#2166)    /// other arrays and array views.*
[2167](https://docs.rs#2167)    ///
[2168](https://docs.rs#2168)    /// Transform the array into `shape`; any shape with the same number of
[2169](https://docs.rs#2169)    /// elements is accepted.
[2170](https://docs.rs#2170)    ///
[2171](https://docs.rs#2171)    /// May clone all elements if needed to arrange elements in standard
[2172](https://docs.rs#2172)    /// layout (and break sharing).
[2173](https://docs.rs#2173)    ///
[2174](https://docs.rs#2174)    /// **Panics** if shapes are incompatible.
[2175](https://docs.rs#2175)    ///
[2176](https://docs.rs#2176)    /// *This method is obsolete, because it is inflexible in how logical order

[2183](https://docs.rs#2183)    ///     rcarr1(&[1., 2., 3., 4.]).reshape((2, 2))
[2184](https://docs.rs#2184)    ///     == rcarr2(&[[1., 2.],
[2185](https://docs.rs#2185)    ///                 [3., 4.]])
[2186](https://docs.rs#2186)    /// );
[2187](https://docs.rs#2187)    /// ```
[2188](https://docs.rs#2188)    #[track_caller]
[2189](https://docs.rs#2189)    #[deprecated(note = "Use `.into_shape_with_order()` or `.to_shape()`", since = "0.16.0")]
[2190](https://docs.rs#2190)    pub fn reshape<E>(&self, shape: E) -> ArrayBase<S, E::Dim>
[2191](https://docs.rs#2191)    where
[2192](https://docs.rs#2192)        S: DataShared + DataOwned,
[2193](https://docs.rs#2193)        A: Clone,
[2194](https://docs.rs#2194)        E: IntoDimension,
[2195](https://docs.rs#2195)    {
[2196](https://docs.rs#2196)        let shape = shape.into_dimension();
[2197](https://docs.rs#2197)        if size_of_shape_checked(&shape) != Ok(self._dim().size()) {
[2198](https://docs.rs#2198)            panic!(
[2199](https://docs.rs#2199)                "ndarray: incompatible shapes in reshape, attempted from: {:?}, to: {:?}",
[2200](https://docs.rs#2200)                self._dim().slice(),
[2201](https://docs.rs#2201)                shape.slice()
[2202](https://docs.rs#2202)            )
[2203](https://docs.rs#2203)        }
[2204](https://docs.rs#2204)        // Check if contiguous, if not => copy all, else just adapt strides
[2205](https://docs.rs#2205)        if self.is_standard_layout() {
[2206](https://docs.rs#2206)            let cl = self.clone();
[2207](https://docs.rs#2207)            // safe because array is contiguous and shape has equal number of elements
[2208](https://docs.rs#2208)            unsafe { cl.with_strides_dim(shape.default_strides(), shape) }
[2209](https://docs.rs#2209)        } else {
[2210](https://docs.rs#2210)            let v = self.iter().cloned().collect::<Vec<A>>();
[2211](https://docs.rs#2211)            unsafe { ArrayBase::from_shape_vec_unchecked(shape, v) }
[2212](https://docs.rs#2212)        }
[2213](https://docs.rs#2213)    }

[2311](https://docs.rs#2311)    /// // (Ix2 dimension type).
[2312](https://docs.rs#2312)    ///
[2313](https://docs.rs#2313)    /// let array = ArrayD::<f64>::zeros(IxDyn(&[10, 10]));
[2314](https://docs.rs#2314)    ///
[2315](https://docs.rs#2315)    /// assert!(array.into_dimensionality::<Ix2>().is_ok());
[2316](https://docs.rs#2316)    /// ```
[2317](https://docs.rs#2317)    pub fn into_dimensionality<D2>(self) -> Result<ArrayBase<S, D2>, ShapeError>
[2318](https://docs.rs#2318)    where D2: Dimension
[2319](https://docs.rs#2319)    {
[2320](https://docs.rs#2320)        unsafe {
[2321](https://docs.rs#2321)            if D::NDIM == D2::NDIM {
[2322](https://docs.rs#2322)                // safe because D == D2
[2323](https://docs.rs#2323)                let dim = unlimited_transmute::<D, D2>(self.parts.dim);
[2324](https://docs.rs#2324)                let strides = unlimited_transmute::<D, D2>(self.parts.strides);
[2325](https://docs.rs#2325)                return Ok(ArrayBase::from_data_ptr(self.data, self.parts.ptr).with_strides_dim(strides, dim));
[2326](https://docs.rs#2326)            } else if D::NDIM.is_none() || D2::NDIM.is_none() {
[2327](https://docs.rs#2327)                // one is dynamic dim
[2328](https://docs.rs#2328)                // safe because dim, strides are equivalent under a different type
[2329](https://docs.rs#2329)                if let Some(dim) = D2::from_dimension(&self.parts.dim) {
[2330](https://docs.rs#2330)                    if let Some(strides) = D2::from_dimension(&self.parts.strides) {
[2331](https://docs.rs#2331)                        return Ok(self.with_strides_dim(strides, dim));
[2332](https://docs.rs#2332)                    }
[2333](https://docs.rs#2333)                }
[2334](https://docs.rs#2334)            }
[2335](https://docs.rs#2335)        }
[2336](https://docs.rs#2336)        Err(ShapeError::from_kind(ErrorKind::IncompatibleShape))
[2337](https://docs.rs#2337)    }

[2342](https://docs.rs#2342)    /// Act like a larger size and/or shape array by *broadcasting*
[2343](https://docs.rs#2343)    /// into a larger shape, if possible.
[2344](https://docs.rs#2344)    ///
[2345](https://docs.rs#2345)    /// Return `None` if shapes can not be broadcast together.
[2346](https://docs.rs#2346)    ///
[2347](https://docs.rs#2347)    /// ***Background***
[2348](https://docs.rs#2348)    ///
[2349](https://docs.rs#2349)    ///  * Two axes are compatible if they are equal, or one of them is 1.
[2350](https://docs.rs#2350)    ///  * In this instance, only the axes of the smaller side (self) can be 1.
[2351](https://docs.rs#2351)    ///
[2352](https://docs.rs#2352)    /// Compare axes beginning with the *last* axis of each shape.
[2353](https://docs.rs#2353)    ///
[2354](https://docs.rs#2354)    /// For example (1, 2, 4) can be broadcast into (7, 6, 2, 4)
[2355](https://docs.rs#2355)    /// because its axes are either equal or 1 (or missing);
[2356](https://docs.rs#2356)    /// while (2, 2) can *not* be broadcast into (2, 4).
[2357](https://docs.rs#2357)    ///
[2358](https://docs.rs#2358)    /// The implementation creates a view with strides set to zero for the
[2359](https://docs.rs#2359)    /// axes that are to be repeated.
[2360](https://docs.rs#2360)    ///
[2361](https://docs.rs#2361)    /// The broadcasting documentation for NumPy has more information.
[2362](https://docs.rs#2362)    ///
[2363](https://docs.rs#2363)    /// ```
[2364](https://docs.rs#2364)    /// use ndarray::{aview1, aview2};
[2365](https://docs.rs#2365)    ///
[2366](https://docs.rs#2366)    /// assert!(
[2367](https://docs.rs#2367)    ///     aview1(&[1., 0.]).broadcast((10, 2)).unwrap()
[2368](https://docs.rs#2368)    ///     == aview2(&[[1., 0.]; 10])
[2369](https://docs.rs#2369)    /// );
[2370](https://docs.rs#2370)    /// ```
[2371](https://docs.rs#2371)    pub fn broadcast<E>(&self, dim: E) -> Option<ArrayView<'_, A, E::Dim>>
[2372](https://docs.rs#2372)    where E: IntoDimension
[2373](https://docs.rs#2373)    {
[2374](https://docs.rs#2374)        /// Return new stride when trying to grow `from` into shape `to`
[2375](https://docs.rs#2375)        ///
[2376](https://docs.rs#2376)        /// Broadcasting works by returning a "fake stride" where elements
[2377](https://docs.rs#2377)        /// to repeat are in axes with 0 stride, so that several indexes point
[2378](https://docs.rs#2378)        /// to the same element.
[2379](https://docs.rs#2379)        ///
[2380](https://docs.rs#2380)        /// **Note:** Cannot be used for mutable iterators, since repeating
[2381](https://docs.rs#2381)        /// elements would create aliasing pointers.
[2382](https://docs.rs#2382)        fn upcast<D: Dimension, E: Dimension>(to: &D, from: &E, stride: &E) -> Option<D>
[2383](https://docs.rs#2383)        {
[2384](https://docs.rs#2384)            // Make sure the product of non-zero axis lengths does not exceed
[2385](https://docs.rs#2385)            // `isize::MAX`. This is the only safety check we need to perform
[2386](https://docs.rs#2386)            // because all the other constraints of `ArrayBase` are guaranteed
[2387](https://docs.rs#2387)            // to be met since we're starting from a valid `ArrayBase`.
[2388](https://docs.rs#2388)            let _ = size_of_shape_checked(to).ok()?;
[2389](https://docs.rs#2389)
[2390](https://docs.rs#2390)            let mut new_stride = to.clone();
[2391](https://docs.rs#2391)            // begin at the back (the least significant dimension)
[2392](https://docs.rs#2392)            // size of the axis has to either agree or `from` has to be 1
[2393](https://docs.rs#2393)            if to.ndim() < from.ndim() {
[2394](https://docs.rs#2394)                return None;
[2395](https://docs.rs#2395)            }
[2396](https://docs.rs#2396)
[2397](https://docs.rs#2397)            {
[2398](https://docs.rs#2398)                let mut new_stride_iter = new_stride.slice_mut().iter_mut().rev();
[2399](https://docs.rs#2399)                for ((er, es), dr) in from
[2400](https://docs.rs#2400)                    .slice()
[2401](https://docs.rs#2401)                    .iter()
[2402](https://docs.rs#2402)                    .rev()
[2403](https://docs.rs#2403)                    .zip(stride.slice().iter().rev())
[2404](https://docs.rs#2404)                    .zip(new_stride_iter.by_ref())
[2405](https://docs.rs#2405)                {
[2406](https://docs.rs#2406)                    /* update strides */
[2407](https://docs.rs#2407)                    if *dr == *er {
[2408](https://docs.rs#2408)                        /* keep stride */
[2409](https://docs.rs#2409)                        *dr = *es;
[2410](https://docs.rs#2410)                    } else if *er == 1 {
[2411](https://docs.rs#2411)                        /* dead dimension, zero stride */
[2412](https://docs.rs#2412)                        *dr = 0
[2413](https://docs.rs#2413)                    } else {
[2414](https://docs.rs#2414)                        return None;
[2415](https://docs.rs#2415)                    }
[2416](https://docs.rs#2416)                }
[2417](https://docs.rs#2417)
[2418](https://docs.rs#2418)                /* set remaining strides to zero */
[2419](https://docs.rs#2419)                for dr in new_stride_iter {
[2420](https://docs.rs#2420)                    *dr = 0;
[2421](https://docs.rs#2421)                }
[2422](https://docs.rs#2422)            }
[2423](https://docs.rs#2423)            Some(new_stride)
[2424](https://docs.rs#2424)        }
[2425](https://docs.rs#2425)        let dim = dim.into_dimension();
[2426](https://docs.rs#2426)
[2427](https://docs.rs#2427)        // Note: zero strides are safe precisely because we return an read-only view
[2428](https://docs.rs#2428)        let broadcast_strides = upcast(&dim, self._dim(), self._strides())?;
[2429](https://docs.rs#2429)        unsafe { Some(ArrayView::new(*self._ptr(), dim, broadcast_strides)) }
[2430](https://docs.rs#2430)    }
[2431](https://docs.rs#2431)
[2432](https://docs.rs#2432)    /// For two arrays or views, find their common shape if possible and
[2433](https://docs.rs#2433)    /// broadcast them as array views into that shape.
[2434](https://docs.rs#2434)    ///
[2435](https://docs.rs#2435)    /// Return `ShapeError` if their shapes can not be broadcast together.
[2436](https://docs.rs#2436)    #[allow(clippy::type_complexity)]
[2437](https://docs.rs#2437)    pub(crate) fn broadcast_with<'a, 'b, B, E>(
[2438](https://docs.rs#2438)        &'a self, other: &'b ArrayRef<B, E>,
[2439](https://docs.rs#2439)    ) -> Result<(ArrayView<'a, A, DimMaxOf<D, E>>, ArrayView<'b, B, DimMaxOf<D, E>>), ShapeError>
[2440](https://docs.rs#2440)    where
[2441](https://docs.rs#2441)        D: Dimension + DimMax<E>,
[2442](https://docs.rs#2442)        E: Dimension,
[2443](https://docs.rs#2443)    {
[2444](https://docs.rs#2444)        let shape = co_broadcast::<D, E, <D as DimMax<E>>::Output>(self._dim(), other._dim())?;
[2445](https://docs.rs#2445)        let view1 = if shape.slice() == self._dim().slice() {
[2446](https://docs.rs#2446)            self.view()
[2447](https://docs.rs#2447)                .into_dimensionality::<<D as DimMax<E>>::Output>()
[2448](https://docs.rs#2448)                .unwrap()
[2449](https://docs.rs#2449)        } else if let Some(view1) = self.broadcast(shape.clone()) {
[2450](https://docs.rs#2450)            view1
[2451](https://docs.rs#2451)        } else {
[2452](https://docs.rs#2452)            return Err(from_kind(ErrorKind::IncompatibleShape));
[2453](https://docs.rs#2453)        };
[2454](https://docs.rs#2454)        let view2 = if shape.slice() == other._dim().slice() {
[2455](https://docs.rs#2455)            other
[2456](https://docs.rs#2456)                .view()
[2457](https://docs.rs#2457)                .into_dimensionality::<<D as DimMax<E>>::Output>()
[2458](https://docs.rs#2458)                .unwrap()
[2459](https://docs.rs#2459)        } else if let Some(view2) = other.broadcast(shape) {
[2460](https://docs.rs#2460)            view2
[2461](https://docs.rs#2461)        } else {
[2462](https://docs.rs#2462)            return Err(from_kind(ErrorKind::IncompatibleShape));
[2463](https://docs.rs#2463)        };
[2464](https://docs.rs#2464)        Ok((view1, view2))
[2465](https://docs.rs#2465)    }
[2466](https://docs.rs#2466)}
[2467](https://docs.rs#2467)
[2468](https://docs.rs#2468)impl<A, D: Dimension> LayoutRef<A, D>
[2469](https://docs.rs#2469){
[2470](https://docs.rs#2470)    /// Swap axes `ax` and `bx`.
[2471](https://docs.rs#2471)    ///
[2472](https://docs.rs#2472)    /// This does not move any data, it just adjusts the array’s dimensions
[2473](https://docs.rs#2473)    /// and strides.
[2474](https://docs.rs#2474)    ///
[2475](https://docs.rs#2475)    /// **Panics** if the axes are out of bounds.
[2476](https://docs.rs#2476)    ///
[2477](https://docs.rs#2477)    /// ```
[2478](https://docs.rs#2478)    /// use ndarray::arr2;
[2479](https://docs.rs#2479)    ///
[2480](https://docs.rs#2480)    /// let mut a = arr2(&[[1., 2., 3.]]);
[2481](https://docs.rs#2481)    /// a.swap_axes(0, 1);
[2482](https://docs.rs#2482)    /// assert!(
[2483](https://docs.rs#2483)    ///     a == arr2(&[[1.], [2.], [3.]])
[2484](https://docs.rs#2484)    /// );
[2485](https://docs.rs#2485)    /// ```
[2486](https://docs.rs#2486)    #[track_caller]
[2487](https://docs.rs#2487)    pub fn swap_axes(&mut self, ax: usize, bx: usize)
[2488](https://docs.rs#2488)    {
[2489](https://docs.rs#2489)        self.0.dim.slice_mut().swap(ax, bx);
[2490](https://docs.rs#2490)        self.0.strides.slice_mut().swap(ax, bx);
[2491](https://docs.rs#2491)    }
[2492](https://docs.rs#2492)}
[2493](https://docs.rs#2493)
[2494](https://docs.rs#2494)impl<A, S, D> ArrayBase<S, D>
[2495](https://docs.rs#2495)where
[2496](https://docs.rs#2496)    S: RawData<Elem = A>,
[2497](https://docs.rs#2497)    D: Dimension,
[2498](https://docs.rs#2498){
[2499](https://docs.rs#2499)    /// Permute the axes.
[2500](https://docs.rs#2500)    ///
[2501](https://docs.rs#2501)    /// This does not move any data, it just adjusts the array’s dimensions
[2502](https://docs.rs#2502)    /// and strides.
[2503](https://docs.rs#2503)    ///
[2504](https://docs.rs#2504)    /// *i* in the *j*-th place in the axes sequence means `self`'s *i*-th axis
[2505](https://docs.rs#2505)    /// becomes `self.permuted_axes()`'s *j*-th axis
[2506](https://docs.rs#2506)    ///
[2507](https://docs.rs#2507)    /// **Panics** if any of the axes are out of bounds, if an axis is missing,
[2508](https://docs.rs#2508)    /// or if an axis is repeated more than once.
[2509](https://docs.rs#2509)    ///
[2510](https://docs.rs#2510)    /// # Examples
[2511](https://docs.rs#2511)    ///
[2512](https://docs.rs#2512)    /// ```
[2513](https://docs.rs#2513)    /// use ndarray::{arr2, Array3};
[2514](https://docs.rs#2514)    ///
[2515](https://docs.rs#2515)    /// let a = arr2(&[[0, 1], [2, 3]]);
[2516](https://docs.rs#2516)    /// assert_eq!(a.view().permuted_axes([1, 0]), a.t());
[2517](https://docs.rs#2517)    ///
[2518](https://docs.rs#2518)    /// let b = Array3::<u8>::zeros((1, 2, 3));
[2519](https://docs.rs#2519)    /// assert_eq!(b.permuted_axes([1, 0, 2]).shape(), &[2, 1, 3]);
[2520](https://docs.rs#2520)    /// ```
[2521](https://docs.rs#2521)    #[track_caller]
[2522](https://docs.rs#2522)    pub fn permuted_axes<T>(self, axes: T) -> ArrayBase<S, D>
[2523](https://docs.rs#2523)    where T: IntoDimension<Dim = D>
[2524](https://docs.rs#2524)    {
[2525](https://docs.rs#2525)        let axes = axes.into_dimension();
[2526](https://docs.rs#2526)        // Ensure that each axis is used exactly once.
[2527](https://docs.rs#2527)        let mut usage_counts = D::zeros(self.ndim());
[2528](https://docs.rs#2528)        for axis in axes.slice() {
[2529](https://docs.rs#2529)            usage_counts[*axis] += 1;
[2530](https://docs.rs#2530)        }
[2531](https://docs.rs#2531)        for count in usage_counts.slice() {
[2532](https://docs.rs#2532)            assert_eq!(*count, 1, "each axis must be listed exactly once");
[2533](https://docs.rs#2533)        }
[2534](https://docs.rs#2534)        // Determine the new shape and strides.
[2535](https://docs.rs#2535)        let mut new_dim = usage_counts; // reuse to avoid an allocation
[2536](https://docs.rs#2536)        let mut new_strides = D::zeros(self.ndim());
[2537](https://docs.rs#2537)        {
[2538](https://docs.rs#2538)            let dim = self.parts.dim.slice();
[2539](https://docs.rs#2539)            let strides = self.parts.strides.slice();
[2540](https://docs.rs#2540)            for (new_axis, &axis) in axes.slice().iter().enumerate() {
[2541](https://docs.rs#2541)                new_dim[new_axis] = dim[axis];
[2542](https://docs.rs#2542)                new_strides[new_axis] = strides[axis];
[2543](https://docs.rs#2543)            }
[2544](https://docs.rs#2544)        }
[2545](https://docs.rs#2545)        // safe because axis invariants are checked above; they are a permutation of the old
[2546](https://docs.rs#2546)        unsafe { self.with_strides_dim(new_strides, new_dim) }
[2547](https://docs.rs#2547)    }
[2548](https://docs.rs#2548)
[2549](https://docs.rs#2549)    /// Permute the axes in-place.
[2550](https://docs.rs#2550)    ///
[2551](https://docs.rs#2551)    /// This does not move any data, it just adjusts the array's dimensions
[2552](https://docs.rs#2552)    /// and strides.
[2553](https://docs.rs#2553)    ///
[2554](https://docs.rs#2554)    /// *i* in the *j*-th place in the axes sequence means `self`'s *i*-th axis
[2555](https://docs.rs#2555)    /// becomes `self`'s *j*-th axis
[2556](https://docs.rs#2556)    ///
[2557](https://docs.rs#2557)    /// **Panics** if any of the axes are out of bounds, if an axis is missing,
[2558](https://docs.rs#2558)    /// or if an axis is repeated more than once.
[2559](https://docs.rs#2559)    ///
[2560](https://docs.rs#2560)    /// # Example
[2561](https://docs.rs#2561)    /// ```rust
[2562](https://docs.rs#2562)    /// use ndarray::{arr2, Array3};
[2563](https://docs.rs#2563)    ///
[2564](https://docs.rs#2564)    /// let mut a = arr2(&[[0, 1], [2, 3]]);
[2565](https://docs.rs#2565)    /// a.permute_axes([1, 0]);
[2566](https://docs.rs#2566)    /// assert_eq!(a, arr2(&[[0, 2], [1, 3]]));
[2567](https://docs.rs#2567)    ///
[2568](https://docs.rs#2568)    /// let mut b = Array3::<u8>::zeros((1, 2, 3));
[2569](https://docs.rs#2569)    /// b.permute_axes([1, 0, 2]);
[2570](https://docs.rs#2570)    /// assert_eq!(b.shape(), &[2, 1, 3]);
[2571](https://docs.rs#2571)    /// ```
[2572](https://docs.rs#2572)    #[track_caller]
[2573](https://docs.rs#2573)    pub fn permute_axes<T>(&mut self, axes: T)
[2574](https://docs.rs#2574)    where T: IntoDimension<Dim = D>
[2575](https://docs.rs#2575)    {
[2576](https://docs.rs#2576)        let axes = axes.into_dimension();
[2577](https://docs.rs#2577)        // Ensure that each axis is used exactly once.
[2578](https://docs.rs#2578)        let mut usage_counts = D::zeros(self.ndim());
[2579](https://docs.rs#2579)        for axis in axes.slice() {
[2580](https://docs.rs#2580)            usage_counts[*axis] += 1;
[2581](https://docs.rs#2581)        }
[2582](https://docs.rs#2582)        for count in usage_counts.slice() {
[2583](https://docs.rs#2583)            assert_eq!(*count, 1, "each axis must be listed exactly once");
[2584](https://docs.rs#2584)        }
[2585](https://docs.rs#2585)
[2586](https://docs.rs#2586)        let dim = self.parts.dim.slice_mut();
[2587](https://docs.rs#2587)        let strides = self.parts.strides.slice_mut();
[2588](https://docs.rs#2588)        let axes = axes.slice();
[2589](https://docs.rs#2589)
[2590](https://docs.rs#2590)        // The cycle detection is done using a bitmask to track visited positions.
[2591](https://docs.rs#2591)        // For example, axes from [0,1,2] to [2, 0, 1]
[2592](https://docs.rs#2592)        // For axis values [1, 0, 2]:
[2593](https://docs.rs#2593)        // 1 << 1  // 0b0001 << 1 = 0b0010 (decimal 2)
[2594](https://docs.rs#2594)        // 1 << 0  // 0b0001 << 0 = 0b0001 (decimal 1)
[2595](https://docs.rs#2595)        // 1 << 2  // 0b0001 << 2 = 0b0100 (decimal 4)
[2596](https://docs.rs#2596)        //
[2597](https://docs.rs#2597)        // Each axis gets its own unique bit position in the bitmask:
[2598](https://docs.rs#2598)        // - Axis 0: bit 0 (rightmost)
[2599](https://docs.rs#2599)        // - Axis 1: bit 1
[2600](https://docs.rs#2600)        // - Axis 2: bit 2
[2601](https://docs.rs#2601)        //
[2602](https://docs.rs#2602)        let mut visited = 0usize;
[2603](https://docs.rs#2603)        for (new_axis, &axis) in axes.iter().enumerate() {
[2604](https://docs.rs#2604)            if (visited & (1 << axis)) != 0 {
[2605](https://docs.rs#2605)                continue;
[2606](https://docs.rs#2606)            }
[2607](https://docs.rs#2607)
[2608](https://docs.rs#2608)            dim.swap(axis, new_axis);
[2609](https://docs.rs#2609)            strides.swap(axis, new_axis);
[2610](https://docs.rs#2610)
[2611](https://docs.rs#2611)            visited |= (1 << axis) | (1 << new_axis);
[2612](https://docs.rs#2612)        }
[2613](https://docs.rs#2613)    }
[2614](https://docs.rs#2614)
[2615](https://docs.rs#2615)    /// Transpose the array by reversing axes.
[2616](https://docs.rs#2616)    ///
[2617](https://docs.rs#2617)    /// Transposition reverses the order of the axes (dimensions and strides)
[2618](https://docs.rs#2618)    /// while retaining the same data.
[2619](https://docs.rs#2619)    pub fn reversed_axes(mut self) -> ArrayBase<S, D>
[2620](https://docs.rs#2620)    {
[2621](https://docs.rs#2621)        self.parts.dim.slice_mut().reverse();
[2622](https://docs.rs#2622)        self.parts.strides.slice_mut().reverse();
[2623](https://docs.rs#2623)        self
[2624](https://docs.rs#2624)    }
[2625](https://docs.rs#2625)
[2626](https://docs.rs#2626)    /// Reverse the axes of the array in-place.
[2627](https://docs.rs#2627)    ///

[2633](https://docs.rs#2633)        self.parts.strides.slice_mut().reverse();

[2672](https://docs.rs#2672)    /// Reverse the stride of `axis`.
[2673](https://docs.rs#2673)    ///
[2674](https://docs.rs#2674)    /// ***Panics*** if the axis is out of bounds.
[2675](https://docs.rs#2675)    #[track_caller]
[2676](https://docs.rs#2676)    pub fn invert_axis(&mut self, axis: Axis)
[2677](https://docs.rs#2677)    {
[2678](https://docs.rs#2678)        unsafe {
[2679](https://docs.rs#2679)            let s = self._strides().axis(axis) as Ixs;
[2680](https://docs.rs#2680)            let m = self._dim().axis(axis);
[2681](https://docs.rs#2681)            if m != 0 {
[2682](https://docs.rs#2682)                self.0.ptr = self._ptr().offset(stride_offset(m - 1, s as Ix));
[2683](https://docs.rs#2683)            }
[2684](https://docs.rs#2684)            self.0.strides.set_axis(axis, (-s) as Ix);
[2685](https://docs.rs#2685)        }
[2686](https://docs.rs#2686)    }
[2687](https://docs.rs#2687)
[2688](https://docs.rs#2688)    /// If possible, merge in the axis `take` to `into`.
[2689](https://docs.rs#2689)    ///
[2690](https://docs.rs#2690)    /// Returns `true` iff the axes are now merged.
[2691](https://docs.rs#2691)    ///
[2692](https://docs.rs#2692)    /// This method merges the axes if movement along the two original axes
[2693](https://docs.rs#2693)    /// (moving fastest along the `into` axis) can be equivalently represented
[2694](https://docs.rs#2694)    /// as movement along one (merged) axis. Merging the axes preserves this
[2695](https://docs.rs#2695)    /// order in the merged axis. If `take` and `into` are the same axis, then
[2696](https://docs.rs#2696)    /// the axis is "merged" if its length is ≤ 1.
[2697](https://docs.rs#2697)    ///
[2698](https://docs.rs#2698)    /// If the return value is `true`, then the following hold:
[2699](https://docs.rs#2699)    ///
[2700](https://docs.rs#2700)    /// * The new length of the `into` axis is the product of the original
[2701](https://docs.rs#2701)    ///   lengths of the two axes.
[2702](https://docs.rs#2702)    ///
[2703](https://docs.rs#2703)    /// * The new length of the `take` axis is 0 if the product of the original
[2704](https://docs.rs#2704)    ///   lengths of the two axes is 0, and 1 otherwise.
[2705](https://docs.rs#2705)    ///
[2706](https://docs.rs#2706)    /// If the return value is `false`, then merging is not possible, and the
[2707](https://docs.rs#2707)    /// original shape and strides have been preserved.
[2708](https://docs.rs#2708)    ///
[2709](https://docs.rs#2709)    /// Note that the ordering constraint means that if it's possible to merge
[2710](https://docs.rs#2710)    /// `take` into `into`, it's usually not possible to merge `into` into
[2711](https://docs.rs#2711)    /// `take`, and vice versa.
[2712](https://docs.rs#2712)    ///
[2713](https://docs.rs#2713)    /// ```
[2714](https://docs.rs#2714)    /// use ndarray::Array3;
[2715](https://docs.rs#2715)    /// use ndarray::Axis;
[2716](https://docs.rs#2716)    ///
[2717](https://docs.rs#2717)    /// let mut a = Array3::<f64>::zeros((2, 3, 4));
[2718](https://docs.rs#2718)    /// assert!(a.merge_axes(Axis(1), Axis(2)));
[2719](https://docs.rs#2719)    /// assert_eq!(a.shape(), &[2, 1, 12]);
[2720](https://docs.rs#2720)    /// ```
[2721](https://docs.rs#2721)    ///
[2722](https://docs.rs#2722)    /// ***Panics*** if an axis is out of bounds.
[2723](https://docs.rs#2723)    #[track_caller]
[2724](https://docs.rs#2724)    pub fn merge_axes(&mut self, take: Axis, into: Axis) -> bool
[2725](https://docs.rs#2725)    {
[2726](https://docs.rs#2726)        let parts = &mut self.0;
[2727](https://docs.rs#2727)        merge_axes(&mut parts.dim, &mut parts.strides, take, into)
[2728](https://docs.rs#2728)    }
[2729](https://docs.rs#2729)}

[2738](https://docs.rs#2738)    /// ```
[2739](https://docs.rs#2739)    /// use ndarray::{Array3, Axis, arr1, arr2};
[2740](https://docs.rs#2740)    ///
[2741](https://docs.rs#2741)    /// // Convert a 1-D array into a row vector (2-D).
[2742](https://docs.rs#2742)    /// let a = arr1(&[1, 2, 3]);
[2743](https://docs.rs#2743)    /// let row = a.insert_axis(Axis(0));
[2744](https://docs.rs#2744)    /// assert_eq!(row, arr2(&[[1, 2, 3]]));

[2746](https://docs.rs#2746)    /// // Convert a 1-D array into a column vector (2-D).
[2747](https://docs.rs#2747)    /// let b = arr1(&[1, 2, 3]);
[2748](https://docs.rs#2748)    /// let col = b.insert_axis(Axis(1));

[2753](https://docs.rs#2753)    /// assert_eq!(b.insert_axis(Axis(2)).shape(), &[3, 4, 1, 5]);

[2756](https://docs.rs#2756)    /// ***Panics*** if the axis is out of bounds.
[2757](https://docs.rs#2757)    #[track_caller]
[2758](https://docs.rs#2758)    pub fn insert_axis(self, axis: Axis) -> ArrayBase<S, D::Larger>
[2759](https://docs.rs#2759)    {
[2760](https://docs.rs#2760)        assert!(axis.index() <= self.ndim());
[2761](https://docs.rs#2761)        // safe because a new axis of length one does not affect memory layout
[2762](https://docs.rs#2762)        unsafe {
[2763](https://docs.rs#2763)            let strides = self.parts.strides.insert_axis(axis);
[2764](https://docs.rs#2764)            let dim = self.parts.dim.insert_axis(axis);
[2765](https://docs.rs#2765)            self.with_strides_dim(strides, dim)
[2766](https://docs.rs#2766)        }
[2767](https://docs.rs#2767)    }

[2825](https://docs.rs#2825)    pub(crate) fn zip_mut_with_same_shape<B, E, F>(&mut self, rhs: &ArrayRef<B, E>, mut f: F)
[2826](https://docs.rs#2826)    where
[2827](https://docs.rs#2827)        E: Dimension,
[2828](https://docs.rs#2828)        F: FnMut(&mut A, &B),

[2830](https://docs.rs#2830)        debug_assert_eq!(self.shape(), rhs.shape());
[2831](https://docs.rs#2831)
[2832](https://docs.rs#2832)        if self
[2833](https://docs.rs#2833)            ._dim()
[2834](https://docs.rs#2834)            .strides_equivalent(self._strides(), rhs._strides())
[2835](https://docs.rs#2835)        {
[2836](https://docs.rs#2836)            if let Some(self_s) = self.as_slice_memory_order_mut() {

[2838](https://docs.rs#2838)                    for (s, r) in self_s.iter_mut().zip(rhs_s) {

[2842](https://docs.rs#2842)                }
[2843](https://docs.rs#2843)            }
[2844](https://docs.rs#2844)        }
[2845](https://docs.rs#2845)
[2846](https://docs.rs#2846)        // Otherwise, fall back to the outer iter
[2847](https://docs.rs#2847)        self.zip_mut_with_by_rows(rhs, f);

[2852](https://docs.rs#2852)    fn zip_mut_with_by_rows<B, E, F>(&mut self, rhs: &ArrayRef<B, E>, mut f: F)
[2853](https://docs.rs#2853)    where
[2854](https://docs.rs#2854)        E: Dimension,

[2858](https://docs.rs#2858)        debug_assert_ne!(self.ndim(), 0);
[2859](https://docs.rs#2859)
[2860](https://docs.rs#2860)        // break the arrays up into their inner rows
[2861](https://docs.rs#2861)        let n = self.ndim();
[2862](https://docs.rs#2862)        let dim = self.raw_dim();
[2863](https://docs.rs#2863)        Zip::from(LanesMut::new(self.view_mut(), Axis(n - 1)))
[2864](https://docs.rs#2864)            .and(Lanes::new(rhs.broadcast_assume(dim), Axis(n - 1)))
[2865](https://docs.rs#2865)            .for_each(move |s_row, r_row| Zip::from(s_row).and(r_row).for_each(&mut f));
[2866](https://docs.rs#2866)    }

[2874](https://docs.rs#2874)    /// Traverse two arrays in unspecified order, in lock step,

[2876](https://docs.rs#2876)    ///
[2877](https://docs.rs#2877)    /// If their shapes disagree, `rhs` is broadcast to the shape of `self`.
[2878](https://docs.rs#2878)    ///
[2879](https://docs.rs#2879)    /// **Panics** if broadcasting isn’t possible.
[2880](https://docs.rs#2880)    #[track_caller]
[2881](https://docs.rs#2881)    #[inline]
[2882](https://docs.rs#2882)    pub fn zip_mut_with<B, E, F>(&mut self, rhs: &ArrayRef<B, E>, f: F)
[2883](https://docs.rs#2883)    where
[2884](https://docs.rs#2884)        E: Dimension,
[2885](https://docs.rs#2885)        F: FnMut(&mut A, &B),
[2886](https://docs.rs#2886)    {
[2887](https://docs.rs#2887)        if rhs._dim().ndim() == 0 {
[2888](https://docs.rs#2888)            // Skip broadcast from 0-dim array
[2889](https://docs.rs#2889)            self.zip_mut_with_elem(rhs.get_0d(), f);
[2890](https://docs.rs#2890)        } else if self._dim().ndim() == rhs._dim().ndim() && self.shape() == rhs.shape() {
[2891](https://docs.rs#2891)            self.zip_mut_with_same_shape(rhs, f);
[2892](https://docs.rs#2892)        } else {
[2893](https://docs.rs#2893)            let rhs_broadcast = rhs.broadcast_unwrap(self.raw_dim());
[2894](https://docs.rs#2894)            self.zip_mut_with_by_rows(&rhs_broadcast, f);
[2895](https://docs.rs#2895)        }
[2896](https://docs.rs#2896)    }

[2911](https://docs.rs#2911)            move_min_stride_axis_to_last(&mut v.parts.dim, &mut v.parts.strides);

[3018](https://docs.rs#3018)    /// Consume the array, call `f` by **v**alue on each element, and return an
[3019](https://docs.rs#3019)    /// owned array with the new values. Works for **any** `F: FnMut(A)->B`.
[3020](https://docs.rs#3020)    ///
[3021](https://docs.rs#3021)    /// If `A` and `B` are the same type then the map is performed by delegating
[3022](https://docs.rs#3022)    /// to [`mapv_into`] and then converting into an owned array. This avoids
[3023](https://docs.rs#3023)    /// unnecessary memory allocations in [`mapv`].
[3024](https://docs.rs#3024)    ///
[3025](https://docs.rs#3025)    /// If `A` and `B` are different types then a new array is allocated and the
[3026](https://docs.rs#3026)    /// map is performed as in [`mapv`].
[3027](https://docs.rs#3027)    ///
[3028](https://docs.rs#3028)    /// Elements are visited in arbitrary order.
[3029](https://docs.rs#3029)    ///
[3030](https://docs.rs#3030)    /// [`mapv_into`]: ArrayBase::mapv_into
[3031](https://docs.rs#3031)    /// [`mapv`]: ArrayRef::mapv
[3032](https://docs.rs#3032)    pub fn mapv_into_any<B, F>(self, mut f: F) -> Array<B, D>
[3033](https://docs.rs#3033)    where
[3034](https://docs.rs#3034)        S: DataMut,
[3035](https://docs.rs#3035)        F: FnMut(A) -> B,
[3036](https://docs.rs#3036)        A: Clone + 'static,
[3037](https://docs.rs#3037)        B: 'static,
[3038](https://docs.rs#3038)    {
[3039](https://docs.rs#3039)        if core::any::TypeId::of::<A>() == core::any::TypeId::of::<B>() {
[3040](https://docs.rs#3040)            // A and B are the same type.
[3041](https://docs.rs#3041)            // Wrap f in a closure of type FnMut(A) -> A .
[3042](https://docs.rs#3042)            let f = |a| {
[3043](https://docs.rs#3043)                let b = f(a);
[3044](https://docs.rs#3044)                // Safe because A and B are the same type.
[3045](https://docs.rs#3045)                unsafe { unlimited_transmute::<B, A>(b) }
[3046](https://docs.rs#3046)            };
[3047](https://docs.rs#3047)            // Delegate to mapv_into() using the wrapped closure.
[3048](https://docs.rs#3048)            // Convert output to a uniquely owned array of type Array<A, D>.
[3049](https://docs.rs#3049)            let output = self.mapv_into(f).into_owned();
[3050](https://docs.rs#3050)            // Change the return type from Array<A, D> to Array<B, D>.
[3051](https://docs.rs#3051)            // Again, safe because A and B are the same type.
[3052](https://docs.rs#3052)            unsafe { unlimited_transmute::<Array<A, D>, Array<B, D>>(output) }
[3053](https://docs.rs#3053)        } else {
[3054](https://docs.rs#3054)            // A and B are not the same type.
[3055](https://docs.rs#3055)            // Fallback to mapv().
[3056](https://docs.rs#3056)            self.mapv(f)
[3057](https://docs.rs#3057)        }
[3058](https://docs.rs#3058)    }

[3197](https://docs.rs#3197)    ///

[3199](https://docs.rs#3199)    ///

[3201](https://docs.rs#3201)    /// ***Panics*** if not `index < self.len_of(axis)`.
[3202](https://docs.rs#3202)    pub fn remove_index(&mut self, axis: Axis, index: usize)
[3203](https://docs.rs#3203)    {
[3204](https://docs.rs#3204)        assert!(index < self.len_of(axis), "index {} must be less than length of Axis({})", index, axis.index());
[3205](https://docs.rs#3205)        let (_, mut tail) = self.view_mut().split_at(axis, index);
[3206](https://docs.rs#3206)        // shift elements to the front
[3207](https://docs.rs#3207)        Zip::from(tail.lanes_mut(axis)).for_each(|mut lane| lane.rotate1_front());

[3209](https://docs.rs#3209)        self.slice_axis_inplace(axis, Slice::new(0, Some(-1), 1));

[3215](https://docs.rs#3215)    /// Iterates over pairs of consecutive elements along the axis.
[3216](https://docs.rs#3216)    ///
[3217](https://docs.rs#3217)    /// The first argument to the closure is an element, and the second
[3218](https://docs.rs#3218)    /// argument is the next element along the axis. Iteration is guaranteed to
[3219](https://docs.rs#3219)    /// proceed in order along the specified axis, but in all other respects
[3220](https://docs.rs#3220)    /// the iteration order is unspecified.
[3221](https://docs.rs#3221)    ///
[3222](https://docs.rs#3222)    /// # Example
[3223](https://docs.rs#3223)    ///
[3224](https://docs.rs#3224)    /// For example, this can be used to compute the cumulative sum along an
[3225](https://docs.rs#3225)    /// axis:
[3226](https://docs.rs#3226)    ///
[3227](https://docs.rs#3227)    /// ```
[3228](https://docs.rs#3228)    /// use ndarray::{array, Axis};
[3229](https://docs.rs#3229)    ///
[3230](https://docs.rs#3230)    /// let mut arr = array![
[3231](https://docs.rs#3231)    ///     [[1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6]],
[3232](https://docs.rs#3232)    ///     [[7, 8], [9, 10], [11, 12]],
[3233](https://docs.rs#3233)    /// ];
[3234](https://docs.rs#3234)    /// arr.accumulate_axis_inplace(Axis(1), |&prev, curr| *curr += prev);
[3235](https://docs.rs#3235)    /// assert_eq!(
[3236](https://docs.rs#3236)    ///     arr,
[3237](https://docs.rs#3237)    ///     array![
[3238](https://docs.rs#3238)    ///         [[1, 2], [4, 6], [9, 12]],
[3239](https://docs.rs#3239)    ///         [[7, 8], [16, 18], [27, 30]],
[3240](https://docs.rs#3240)    ///     ],
[3241](https://docs.rs#3241)    /// );
[3242](https://docs.rs#3242)    /// ```
[3243](https://docs.rs#3243)    pub fn accumulate_axis_inplace<F>(&mut self, axis: Axis, mut f: F)
[3244](https://docs.rs#3244)    where F: FnMut(&A, &mut A)
[3245](https://docs.rs#3245)    {
[3246](https://docs.rs#3246)        if self.len_of(axis) <= 1 {
[3247](https://docs.rs#3247)            return;
[3248](https://docs.rs#3248)        }
[3249](https://docs.rs#3249)        let mut curr = self.raw_view_mut(); // mut borrow of the array here
[3250](https://docs.rs#3250)        let mut prev = curr.raw_view(); // derive further raw views from the same borrow
[3251](https://docs.rs#3251)        prev.slice_axis_inplace(axis, Slice::from(..-1));
[3252](https://docs.rs#3252)        curr.slice_axis_inplace(axis, Slice::from(1..));
[3253](https://docs.rs#3253)        // This implementation relies on `Zip` iterating along `axis` in order.
[3254](https://docs.rs#3254)        Zip::from(prev).and(curr).for_each(|prev, curr| unsafe {
[3255](https://docs.rs#3255)            // These pointer dereferences and borrows are safe because:
[3256](https://docs.rs#3256)            //
[3257](https://docs.rs#3257)            // 1. They're pointers to elements in the array.
[3258](https://docs.rs#3258)            //
[3259](https://docs.rs#3259)            // 2. `S: DataMut` guarantees that elements are safe to borrow
[3260](https://docs.rs#3260)            //    mutably and that they don't alias.
[3261](https://docs.rs#3261)            //
[3262](https://docs.rs#3262)            // 3. The lifetimes of the borrows last only for the duration
[3263](https://docs.rs#3263)            //    of the call to `f`, so aliasing across calls to `f`
[3264](https://docs.rs#3264)            //    cannot occur.
[3265](https://docs.rs#3265)            f(&*prev, &mut *curr)
[3266](https://docs.rs#3266)        });
[3267](https://docs.rs#3267)    }

[3269](https://docs.rs#3269)    /// Return a partitioned copy of the array.
[3270](https://docs.rs#3270)    ///
[3271](https://docs.rs#3271)    /// Creates a copy of the array and partially sorts it around the k-th element along the given axis.
[3272](https://docs.rs#3272)    /// The k-th element will be in its sorted position, with:
[3273](https://docs.rs#3273)    /// - All elements smaller than the k-th element to its left
[3274](https://docs.rs#3274)    /// - All elements equal or greater than the k-th element to its right
[3275](https://docs.rs#3275)    /// - The ordering within each partition is undefined
[3276](https://docs.rs#3276)    ///
[3277](https://docs.rs#3277)    /// Empty arrays (i.e., those with any zero-length axes) are considered partitioned already,
[3278](https://docs.rs#3278)    /// and will be returned unchanged.
[3279](https://docs.rs#3279)    ///
[3280](https://docs.rs#3280)    /// **Panics** if `k` is out of bounds for a non-zero axis length.
[3281](https://docs.rs#3281)    ///
[3282](https://docs.rs#3282)    /// # Parameters
[3283](https://docs.rs#3283)    ///
[3284](https://docs.rs#3284)    /// * `kth` - Index to partition by. The k-th element will be in its sorted position.
[3285](https://docs.rs#3285)    /// * `axis` - Axis along which to partition.
[3286](https://docs.rs#3286)    ///
[3287](https://docs.rs#3287)    /// # Examples
[3288](https://docs.rs#3288)    ///
[3289](https://docs.rs#3289)    /// ```
[3290](https://docs.rs#3290)    /// use ndarray::prelude::*;
[3291](https://docs.rs#3291)    ///
[3292](https://docs.rs#3292)    /// let a = array![7, 1, 5, 2, 6, 0, 3, 4];
[3293](https://docs.rs#3293)    /// let p = a.partition(3, Axis(0));
[3294](https://docs.rs#3294)    ///
[3295](https://docs.rs#3295)    /// // The element at position 3 is now 3, with smaller elements to the left
[3296](https://docs.rs#3296)    /// // and greater elements to the right
[3297](https://docs.rs#3297)    /// assert_eq!(p[3], 3);
[3298](https://docs.rs#3298)    /// assert!(p.slice(s![..3]).iter().all(|&x| x <= 3));
[3299](https://docs.rs#3299)    /// assert!(p.slice(s![4..]).iter().all(|&x| x >= 3));
[3300](https://docs.rs#3300)    /// ```
[3301](https://docs.rs#3301)    pub fn partition(&self, kth: usize, axis: Axis) -> Array<A, D>
[3302](https://docs.rs#3302)    where
[3303](https://docs.rs#3303)        A: Clone + Ord + num_traits::Zero,
[3304](https://docs.rs#3304)        D: Dimension,
[3305](https://docs.rs#3305)    {
[3306](https://docs.rs#3306)        let mut result = self.to_owned();
[3307](https://docs.rs#3307)
[3308](https://docs.rs#3308)        // Return early if the array has zero-length dimensions
[3309](https://docs.rs#3309)        if result.shape().contains(&0) {
[3310](https://docs.rs#3310)            return result;
[3311](https://docs.rs#3311)        }
[3312](https://docs.rs#3312)
[3313](https://docs.rs#3313)        // Bounds checking. Panics if kth is out of bounds
[3314](https://docs.rs#3314)        let axis_len = self.len_of(axis);
[3315](https://docs.rs#3315)        if kth >= axis_len {
[3316](https://docs.rs#3316)            panic!("Partition index {} is out of bounds for axis {} of length {}", kth, axis.0, axis_len);
[3317](https://docs.rs#3317)        }
[3318](https://docs.rs#3318)
[3319](https://docs.rs#3319)        // Check if the first lane is contiguous
[3320](https://docs.rs#3320)        let is_contiguous = result
[3321](https://docs.rs#3321)            .lanes_mut(axis)
[3322](https://docs.rs#3322)            .into_iter()
[3323](https://docs.rs#3323)            .next()
[3324](https://docs.rs#3324)            // This unwrap shouldn't cause panics because the array isn't empty
[3325](https://docs.rs#3325)            .unwrap()
[3326](https://docs.rs#3326)            .is_contiguous();
[3327](https://docs.rs#3327)
[3328](https://docs.rs#3328)        if is_contiguous {
[3329](https://docs.rs#3329)            result.lanes_mut(axis).into_iter().for_each(|mut lane| {
[3330](https://docs.rs#3330)                lane.as_slice_mut().unwrap().select_nth_unstable(kth);
[3331](https://docs.rs#3331)            });
[3332](https://docs.rs#3332)        } else {
[3333](https://docs.rs#3333)            let mut temp_vec = vec![A::zero(); axis_len];
[3334](https://docs.rs#3334)
[3335](https://docs.rs#3335)            Zip::from(result.lanes_mut(axis)).for_each(|mut lane| {
[3336](https://docs.rs#3336)                Zip::from(&mut temp_vec).and(&lane).for_each(|dest, src| {
[3337](https://docs.rs#3337)                    *dest = src.clone();
[3338](https://docs.rs#3338)                });
[3339](https://docs.rs#3339)
[3340](https://docs.rs#3340)                temp_vec.select_nth_unstable(kth);
[3341](https://docs.rs#3341)
[3342](https://docs.rs#3342)                Zip::from(&mut lane).and(&temp_vec).for_each(|dest, src| {
[3343](https://docs.rs#3343)                    *dest = src.clone();
[3344](https://docs.rs#3344)                });
[3345](https://docs.rs#3345)            });
[3346](https://docs.rs#3346)        }
[3347](https://docs.rs#3347)
[3348](https://docs.rs#3348)        result
[3349](https://docs.rs#3349)    }
[3350](https://docs.rs#3350)}
[3351](https://docs.rs#3351)
[3352](https://docs.rs#3352)/// Transmute from A to B.
[3353](https://docs.rs#3353)///
[3354](https://docs.rs#3354)/// Like transmute, but does not have the compile-time size check which blocks
[3355](https://docs.rs#3355)/// using regular transmute in some cases.
[3356](https://docs.rs#3356)///
[3357](https://docs.rs#3357)/// **Panics** if the size of A and B are different.
[3358](https://docs.rs#3358)#[track_caller]
[3359](https://docs.rs#3359)#[inline]
[3360](https://docs.rs#3360)unsafe fn unlimited_transmute<A, B>(data: A) -> B
[3361](https://docs.rs#3361){
[3362](https://docs.rs#3362)    // safe when sizes are equal and caller guarantees that representations are equal
[3363](https://docs.rs#3363)    assert_eq!(size_of::<A>(), size_of::<B>());
[3364](https://docs.rs#3364)    let old_data = ManuallyDrop::new(data);
[3365](https://docs.rs#3365)    (&*old_data as *const A as *const B).read()
[3366](https://docs.rs#3366)}
[3367](https://docs.rs#3367)
[3368](https://docs.rs#3368)type DimMaxOf<A, B> = <A as DimMax<B>>::Output;
[3369](https://docs.rs#3369)

[3457](https://docs.rs#3457)    {
[3458](https://docs.rs#3458)        // Test partitioning a 2D array along both axes
[3459](https://docs.rs#3459)        let array = arr2(&[[3, 1, 4], [1, 5, 9], [2, 6, 5]]);
[3460](https://docs.rs#3460)
[3461](https://docs.rs#3461)        // Partition along axis 0 (rows)
[3462](https://docs.rs#3462)        let result0 = array.partition(1, Axis(0));

[3465](https://docs.rs#3465)        assert!(result0[[0, 1]] <= result0[[1, 1]] && result0[[2, 1]] >= result0[[1, 1]]);
[3466](https://docs.rs#3466)        assert!(result0[[0, 2]] <= result0[[1, 2]] && result0[[2, 2]] >= result0[[1, 2]]);
[3467](https://docs.rs#3467)
[3468](https://docs.rs#3468)        // Partition along axis 1 (columns)
[3469](https://docs.rs#3469)        let result1 = array.partition(1, Axis(1));
[3470](https://docs.rs#3470)        // After partitioning along axis 1, each row should have its middle element in the correct position
[3471](https://docs.rs#3471)        assert!(result1[[0, 0]] <= result1[[0, 1]] && result1[[0, 2]] >= result1[[0, 1]]);
[3472](https://docs.rs#3472)        assert!(result1[[1, 0]] <= result1[[1, 1]] && result1[[1, 2]] >= result1[[1, 1]]);
[3473](https://docs.rs#3473)        assert!(result1[[2, 0]] <= result1[[2, 1]] && result1[[2, 2]] >= result1[[2, 1]]);
[3474](https://docs.rs#3474)    }

[3509](https://docs.rs#3509)    #[test]
[3510](https://docs.rs#3510)    fn test_partition_contiguous_or_not()
[3511](https://docs.rs#3511)    {
[3512](https://docs.rs#3512)        // Test contiguous case (C-order)
[3513](https://docs.rs#3513)        let a = array![[7, 1, 5], [2, 6, 0], [3, 4, 8]];
[3514](https://docs.rs#3514)
[3515](https://docs.rs#3515)        // Partition along axis 0 (contiguous)
[3516](https://docs.rs#3516)        let p_axis0 = a.partition(1, Axis(0));
[3517](https://docs.rs#3517)
[3518](https://docs.rs#3518)        // For each column, verify the partitioning:
[3519](https://docs.rs#3519)        // - First row should be <= middle row (kth element)
[3520](https://docs.rs#3520)        // - Last row should be >= middle row (kth element)
[3521](https://docs.rs#3521)        for col in 0..3 {
[3522](https://docs.rs#3522)            let kth = p_axis0[[1, col]];
[3523](https://docs.rs#3523)            assert!(
[3524](https://docs.rs#3524)                p_axis0[[0, col]] <= kth,
[3525](https://docs.rs#3525)                "Column {}: First row {} should be <= middle row {}",
[3526](https://docs.rs#3526)                col,
[3527](https://docs.rs#3527)                p_axis0[[0, col]],
[3528](https://docs.rs#3528)                kth
[3529](https://docs.rs#3529)            );
[3530](https://docs.rs#3530)            assert!(
[3531](https://docs.rs#3531)                p_axis0[[2, col]] >= kth,
[3532](https://docs.rs#3532)                "Column {}: Last row {} should be >= middle row {}",
[3533](https://docs.rs#3533)                col,
[3534](https://docs.rs#3534)                p_axis0[[2, col]],
[3535](https://docs.rs#3535)                kth
[3536](https://docs.rs#3536)            );
[3537](https://docs.rs#3537)        }
[3538](https://docs.rs#3538)
[3539](https://docs.rs#3539)        // Test non-contiguous case (F-order)
[3540](https://docs.rs#3540)        let a = array![[7, 1, 5], [2, 6, 0], [3, 4, 8]];
[3541](https://docs.rs#3541)
[3542](https://docs.rs#3542)        // Make array non-contiguous by transposing
[3543](https://docs.rs#3543)        let a = a.t().to_owned();
[3544](https://docs.rs#3544)
[3545](https://docs.rs#3545)        // Partition along axis 1 (non-contiguous)
[3546](https://docs.rs#3546)        let p_axis1 = a.partition(1, Axis(1));
[3547](https://docs.rs#3547)
[3548](https://docs.rs#3548)        // For each row, verify the partitioning:
[3549](https://docs.rs#3549)        // - First column should be <= middle column
[3550](https://docs.rs#3550)        // - Last column should be >= middle column
[3551](https://docs.rs#3551)        for row in 0..3 {
[3552](https://docs.rs#3552)            assert!(
[3553](https://docs.rs#3553)                p_axis1[[row, 0]] <= p_axis1[[row, 1]],
[3554](https://docs.rs#3554)                "Row {}: First column {} should be <= middle column {}",
[3555](https://docs.rs#3555)                row,
[3556](https://docs.rs#3556)                p_axis1[[row, 0]],
[3557](https://docs.rs#3557)                p_axis1[[row, 1]]
[3558](https://docs.rs#3558)            );
[3559](https://docs.rs#3559)            assert!(
[3560](https://docs.rs#3560)                p_axis1[[row, 2]] >= p_axis1[[row, 1]],
[3561](https://docs.rs#3561)                "Row {}: Last column {} should be >= middle column {}",
[3562](https://docs.rs#3562)                row,
[3563](https://docs.rs#3563)                p_axis1[[row, 2]],
[3564](https://docs.rs#3564)                p_axis1[[row, 1]]
[3565](https://docs.rs#3565)            );
[3566](https://docs.rs#3566)        }
[3567](https://docs.rs#3567)    }
